name: Motorsport Tech Dive-In — three timed beats with two deliberate cuts, transparent reveal of one hidden system (10 s)
status: owner-approved style 2026-10-26 (3-beat rework: braking hook, locked transparent reveal, corner exit; no five-stage flight)
inspiration: Owner reference reels (GRID MECHANICS style): a real braking moment, a cut to the same assembly seen through transparent bodywork with one airflow path drawn in light, then the car exits the corner; dense fact-based narration from the first second.

generation.narration: spoken by Flow inside the clip; never external TTS

blocks.style: Ultra-realistic cinematic motorsport engineering film, vertical 9:16, clear bright daylight with rich livery and track contrast, controlled highlights, deep focus, film grain; transparent cutaways and glowing flow lines are the only CGI.

clip_templates.prompt: {style} {vehicle} {part_layout} Three shots with two deliberate cuts: [00:00-00:02] {hook_shot} [00:02-00:07] {context_reveal} {macro_detail} {effect_detail} [00:07-00:10] {result_shot} Every glow is soft light inside the parts or in the air, never flames, sparks or smoke; no generated on-screen text, labels, or numbers. Audio: {sound_cues}, low under the voice, no music. {narrator} "{narration_1}"

narration_by_clips.1: narration_1 is continuous from frame 0 without intentional pause across the three beats: it opens with one sourced concrete fact (a number, a temperature, a weight or a rule), then the mechanism, then a plain-language consequence. One or two concrete facts, all from research_notes. Never open with 'This is ...' or a definition.

rules: Pick ONE hidden system that fans wonder about (brakes, gearbox, fuel bag, halo, seat, pit-stop wheel nut, power steering, battery, cooling, mirrors, winglets, rider airbag, tyre heat). The vehicle keeps its normal real shape: never a topic that needs an unusual vehicle layout (six wheels, twin chassis, fan car, gas turbine).

part_layout: one sentence on the real shape of the part, where it is mounted and which way it faces, naming 2 to 4 real components (for example: 'The front-left brake sits inside the front-left wheel: one large carbon disc drilled with many small holes, gripped by one caliper at the top-rear of the disc, with a thin brake line running into the caliper.').

hook_shot [00:00-00:02]: one dramatic braking action with a strong visual hook, the camera already moving (for example a low chase shot of a hard stop into a hairpin, the nose dipping, the camera rising behind the car). One clear shot, no impossible camera flight.

context_reveal + macro_detail + effect_detail together form the middle beat [00:02-00:07]: the camera stays spatially locked on the target assembly; bodywork becomes transparent only around that assembly so every nearby component is clearly visible in its real position; the camera makes one slow stable push toward the part; show one accurate cause/effect path (for example cool airflow from an intake through internal passages, or fluid pressure through a caliper) using the colour code orange = heat, fluid or power, cool blue = air or cooling, amber = force or gears. No labels, no generated text or overlays. Keep other components correctly placed and still.

result_shot [00:07-00:10]: the camera cuts back to the whole vehicle moving forward, controlled braking and corner exit, naming its main parts as unchanged (for a car: 'its front wing, rear wing and sidepods unchanged'); no new trick or effect.
sound_cues: two or three real sounds that match the shots (engine note, hydraulic hiss, mechanical click, rush of air).

Narration: 26-32 words in English (shorter in other languages) so Flow never cuts the last word; it starts at second 0 with a surprising fact, includes one or two numbers or facts only from research_notes, and ends with the consequence or a twist.
Length budgets so the final Flow prompt stays short enough: part_layout at most 170 characters, hook_shot 120, context_reveal 230, macro_detail 230, effect_detail 160, result_shot 140, sound_cues 80.
Never name or show real teams, drivers, riders, makers or sponsors. Do not output livery or channel_name; the system sets them.
keywords_that_worked: Three shots with two deliberate cuts, timed [00:00-00:02] / [00:02-00:07] / [00:07-00:10] (hook braking action, locked transparent reveal with one airflow path, corner exit)
bodywork becomes transparent only around the target assembly; every nearby component clearly visible in place
one slow stable push toward the part, cause/effect airflow or force path
orange = fluid, fuel, heat, power; cool blue = air or cooling; amber = force or gears
no generated on-screen text, labels or numbers; result shot names the main parts as unchanged

f1: carbon brakes: C/C discs exceed a thousand degrees and ducted air passes through internal microchannels
seamless gearbox: hydraulics change gear in milliseconds
the rubber fuel bag behind the driver (verify the current fuel limit)
the halo: about seven kilos that can carry the weight of a bus
the seat moulded to one driver that lifts out with the driver strapped in
the pit-stop wheel nut and the air-powered wheel gun
power steering: hydraulics carry the cornering load
how a driver drinks during the race (verify the litres by regulation)
the battery behind the driver and how much power it adds (verify facts first)
brake ducts: where the cooling air enters and leaves
motogp: the winglets that keep the front wheel down
carbon brakes that only work when they are hot
the rider airbag inside the leather suit
the ride-height device that squats the bike at the start (verify the current rules first)
the seamless gearbox that shifts mid-corner
tyre temperature and the tyre-pressure rule (verify facts first)
the electronics that stop wheelies and slides
the shoulder and knee sliders that touch the asphalt

variables.part_layout: The front-left brake sits inside the front-left wheel: one carbon-carbon disc, one caliper at its top-rear edge, one brake duct feeding air in.
variables.hook_shot: Low rear three-quarter chase shot: the car brakes hard toward a hairpin, nose dipping, the camera rising behind it.
variables.context_reveal: Cut to the front-left wheel area: the bodywork around the brake assembly becomes transparent, revealing the disc, caliper and duct clearly visible inside.
variables.macro_detail: The camera makes one slow stable push toward the brake: orange heat glows from the disc surface, the pads press the spinning disc, and the disc glows brighter.
variables.effect_detail: One path of cool-blue airflow enters the brake duct and passes through internal passages in the disc, carrying heat out while the disc stays hot and glowing.
variables.result_shot: Cut back to the whole car, its front wing, rear wing and sidepods unchanged, completing the corner and accelerating away.
variables.sound_cues: engine note dropping, a hydraulic hiss, rushing cooling air
variables.narration_1: Under heavy braking these carbon-carbon discs can exceed a thousand degrees Celsius. Ducted air passes through internal microchannels inside each disc to pull heat away before it causes brake fade.

questions: which hidden system, and how it works step by step
its real components, their shape, where they are mounted and which way they face
one or two surprising, verifiable numbers (temperature, weight, time, force, a rule)
what it changes on track (the consequence or the twist)

usage: 10 s single clip. Muse writes topic, research_notes and the variables; the system picks a random original livery for the page's niche and uses the page name as the team name.
language: narration in the fan page's language; the template text stays in English
polish_fallback_note: Owner 2026-10-26: when Argon/ChatGPT cannot keep the three timed beats after all attempts, the template's own render is used instead of failing the idea.
